conviction_note: Every candidate edge (the Radiant World fraud at Point Bonita, the September Fed hike and the private-credit overhang, the weak Dealogic Jul-Aug proxy, the rising EPS revisions) is either already in the wire or reflected in the -10.3% 20-day run-up, and the one line that could surprise (asset management) already has a $74m sequential drop from Q2's $187.8m in the $114m consensus, so there is nothing to size and the answer is 0.
bar: Net revenue about $2.20-2.21bn and EPS $1.00-1.04. Two sources agree on revenue: Newsquawk $2.20bn / EPS $1.00 (https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/daily-us-earnings-estimates-28th-september-2026-jef) and Zacks via Yahoo, 2026-09-23, $2.21bn / EPS $1.04, with IB $1.32bn, advisory $813m, equity underwriting $315m, debt underwriting $175m, equities $534m, fixed income $237m, total asset management $114m (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/gear-jefferies-jef-q3-earnings-131522075.html). Jefferies gives no guidance.
positioning_check: Ortex, pre-print (late September 2026): short interest 6.9m shares, 3.4% of free float, up 56%; cost to borrow 0.47%; put/call 2.20 (https://ortex.news/articles/173485/jefferies-heads-into-q3-print-down-9-on-the-month). Days to cover works out to about 3.2 at the baseline's 20-day average volume of 2.18m. This is not a crowded short. Baseline skew is +1.09 vol points, a mild downside lean labelled 'balanced'. Total open interest is thin (3,161). The event-implied move is 7.3%.

outside_window.finding: Jefferies hosts its Investor Day on 2026-10-19. Any multi-year targets or a fuller Point Bonita/Radiant quantification may be held for then rather than given on the 09-28 release.

searched_and_found_nothing: Radiant World / Point Bonita exposure: fraud claim filed 2026-09-08, $499m freezing order 2026-09-02, near-empty coffers 2026-09-17, $870m owed to six lenders with Jefferies' fund among the two largest (2026-09-21). All Bloomberg/FT wire stories after quarter-end, and they coincide with the 10% monthly drawdown. Jefferies' own equity-at-risk is not quantified in any primary document I could reach; the Q2 10-Q text was not readable through WebFetch (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000096223/000009622326000025/jef-20260531.htm). https://www.thewealthadvisor.com/article/jefferies-fund-accuses-radiant-world-500-million-fraud ; https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-21/radiant-world-table-shows-six-lenders-with-870-million-exposure

Asset-management consensus looked stale at first. But Q2 total AM was $187.8m (backed out of the Q2 8-K: net revenue $2,206.5m less IB $1,206.8m, capital markets $799.3m and other $12.6m; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/96223/000009622326000021/jfgpressrelease5312026.htm), so the $114m Q3 consensus already embeds a roughly $74m sequential decline. Not an unpriced miss.

IB fee proxy: a Jefferies research/Dealogic note (2026-09-03) has 8 global banks at -15% YoY and -27% QoQ for calendar Q3 to date (https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/jefferies-investment-banking-fees-down-15-for-major-global-banks-93CH-4856833). It is contradicted by JPMorgan's company-level guide on 2026-09-15 of IB fees up mid-to-high teens YoY (https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-09-15/jpmorgan-expects-investment-banking-trading-shine-third-quarter). BofA guided down 10%+. Peers are mixed and all of this is public, so no net read on Jefferies' $1.32bn IB bar.

ECM: SpaceX's June IPO excluded Jefferies (https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/snubbed-spacex-jefferies-now-helping-traders-short-worlds-biggest-ipo). July US IPOs were $3.0bn. Calendar Q3 IPO proceeds ex-SK hynix were $8.4bn (https://www.renaissancecapital.com/IPO-Center/News/121864/renaissance-capitals-3q-2026-us-ipo-market-review). All public, and the $315m equity underwriting bar sits below Q2's $370.7m.

Oppenheimer raised Q3 IB to $1.274bn and EPS to $1.06 from $0.67 (https://finimize.com/content/jefferies-could-ride-a-deal-making-pickup-oppenheimer-says). Consensus EPS was revised up 8.1% in 30 days. The bar is rising into the print, which is priced by definition.

Hildene 50% acquisition, targeted to close in Q3 FY26 and 'immediately accretive' per the Q2 release. I could not confirm a closing or any remeasurement gain, so nothing to size (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/jefferies-acquire-50-interest-hildene-114500419.html).

SMBC bought 5.9m shares on 2026-07-15 at a final $54.86 (https://www.investing.com/news/insider-trading-news/sumitomo-mitsui-financial-group-buys-3187m-jefferies-stock-93CH-4797883). Known, and not about the print.
September bond issues (6.00% 2030, FRN 2028, 7.00% 2041) look like routine funding for a broker-dealer. No distress signal and no ramp to corroborate.

Fed hike in mid-September 2026 (first since July 2023) and bond yields at a 19-year high: macro hit to financials after quarter-end. Already in the 20-day drawdown, and transmission to Jefferies' Q4 pipeline has not been stated by the company.
baseline_tension: Nothing I found cuts against the baseline. The negatives (Radiant fraud, rate hike, private-credit overhang) are the drawdown itself, and the positives (JPM's IB/markets guide, upward EPS revisions) are wire copy. The price already has all of this, and a reaction history of 1 up in 4 (-9.15% on a record-IB quarter) argues against leaning long on a fundamental beat.
lessons_applied: nothing changed. Lesson 5 (a company-level guide beats an industry proxy) confirmed the pre-lessons decision not to turn the -15% Dealogic proxy into a negative IB finding against JPMorgan's contrary guide. Lesson 7's short-interest check (3.4% of float) found no squeeze mechanism to weigh. With no findings there was nothing to re-size, so the pre and post sums are equal at 0.
